title: Counting with two conditions: COUNTIFS
summary: Count rows that meet two conditions, including a stock band such as 10 to 19 pairs built from two criteria on the same column.

blocks.text: Stock analysts group lines into bands: very low stock, healthy stock and overstock. A band is a range of numbers, such as at least 10 pairs but fewer than 20. Counting a band needs two conditions on the same column.
COUNTIFS counts the rows where every condition is true. Use it for "Nairobi sneakers" (two columns) and for number bands (one column used twice).

items: Objective: count rows with two conditions using COUNTIFS, including a number band.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: Give each condition as a pair: where to look, then what to match. Add more pairs as needed. A row is counted only when all conditions are true. There is no sum range because COUNTIFS counts rows.
Count rows where the region is Nairobi and the pairs in stock are fewer than 10. Only row 2 (8 pairs) qualifies, so the answer is 1.
A number band uses the same range twice, once for the lower limit and once for the upper limit. This counts lines with at least 10 and fewer than 20 pairs.

items: Both conditions must be true on the same row (AND). Two different regions on the same column can never both be true, so that count is 0.
Use >= for the lower limit and < for the upper limit. Then neighbouring bands (0 to <10, 10 to <20, 20 and over) never share a value and nothing is counted twice.
Build band limits from cells with &, for example ">="&F7 and "<"&G7, so you can change a band without editing the formula.

blocks.text: Use the store stock from Training (A1:B8). Type whole numbers, for example 3.

items: COUNTIFS(range1, criteria1, range2, criteria2) counts rows where all conditions are true.
A number band is the same column twice: ">=low" and "<high".
Use >= for the lower limit and < for the upper limit so bands do not overlap.
Build the band limits from cells with & so the bands can be changed easily.

blocks.text: Stock bands built with COUNTIFS give a quick picture of how many lines are low, healthy or overstocked.

items.prompt: Two bands are written ">=10 and <=20" and ">=20 and <=30". What happens to a line with exactly 20 pairs?

options.label: It is counted in both bands
It is counted in neither band
It is counted only in the first band
0, because no cell can be both Nairobi and Mombasa
The number of Nairobi and Mombasa rows together
